_comment: Manual overrides for the 1836 start converter (tools/convert_history.ps1). Each rule targets a vanilla BASE building key, optionally scoped to a country (region_state tag, e.g. 'GBR') and/or state (e.g. 'STATE_HOME_COUNTIES'). action: 'force_tier' sets the factory to tier N (1-based) regardless of its vanilla PM; 'force_industry_tier' re-tiers it onto ANOTHER config industry's tier N (fields: industry, tier) — needed when the target chain is a separate industry whose base building never appears in vanilla history (the steamer chain); 'remove' deletes the factory from the start. Precedence: most specific scope wins (country+state > country > state > none); ties resolved by last rule. Only the 'rules' array is read; '_examples' is ignored. See config/start_baseline.json (generated by tools/extract_start.ps1) for the inventory of what exists to target.
_why_steamer_seed: REVERTED (user-ruled 2026-08-16, same day): the seed existed only to feed the abnormal from-start steam-port construction, which F66 traced to the engine provisioning every overseas state once per port building TYPE — the disease to fix, not the symptom to feed. The force_industry_tier machinery stays (documented, tested); the rules are withdrawn. The five rules it carried: GBR Home Counties 5 / FRA Brittany 4 / USA Virginia 2 / BEL Flanders 1 / PRU West Prussia 1 -> building_shipyard_metal.
_why_chain_seed: THE В§2 CHAIN SEED вЂ” RATIFIED STANDING DESIGN (user-ruled 2026-08-16 late evening + Q5a/Q5c the same night, В§10.60.3): every anchorage in the GBR and FRA 1836 markets (the two markets whose LEADER holds screw_frigate from day 0 - tier-1 starting techs are GBR/FRA/USA/PRU/BEL, of whom only these two have overseas empires) becomes a tier-2 (t1 steam, graded 1/10-size) port stub at level 1 (the anchorage clamp holds it there). LEADER-owned anchorages convert plainly; SUBJECT-owned ones (BIC/SIL/ION/NSW/PLY/MKT/ABU/ORG - Q5a ruled after MEASURING that the engine provisions steam ports into these states regardless of the subject s tech, SIL by 1837.1 in the century run) convert with ownership REWRITTEN TO THE OVERLORD (`owner`) and NO tech grant - covered not by an exception but by the REFINED L14 RULE (user, same night): the starting-tech gate binds DOMESTICALLY-owned buildings only; a building wholly owned by foreign countries rides its owners technology (verify_start_techs.mjs parses each block s ownership and prints the foreign-owned skip count). DEI excluded - NET market, leader lacks the tech at start. Each leader gets ONE metal shipyard by converting a small clipper-shipyard block (GBR East Anglia, FRA Brittany; Q6 sizing rule: ceil(stubs / (yard output/stub demand)) yards, min 1 - one each suffices below ~107 stubs), and FRA one motor factory (Q5c: Rhone 1-lv paper mill -> motor t1; FRA holds atmospheric_engine). STEEL IS NOT SEEDED (GBR Yorkshire 6 lv, FRA Alsace 1 lv exist); leader-owned overseas BASIC-port states (Malta/Gibraltar/Malaya) are NOT seeded - the engine provisions their steam stubs within weeks at graded cost (measured). Regenerate with the gen_seed_rules.mjs pattern (vanilla history anchorages x ui/presets.js market membership).
_why_net_seed: THE SEED, as ruled 2026-08-17 (supersedes every earlier shape). NOTHING IS REPLACED - no replacement was ever intended, and an earlier draft using force_tier CONVERTED 40 anchorages into steam ports, silently deleting their tier-0 clipper port and that clipper demand with it. The design is purely additive: (1) ANCHORAGES STAY as tier-0 clipper ports at level 1, exactly as vanilla places them; (2) a tier-1 STEAM PORT of level 1 is CREATED beside each one, in every eligible overseas state of a seeded market, owned by the market leaders GOVERNMENT - placement is the states own region_state, ownership is the leader, which are different questions; (3) where the market would otherwise carry steamer/motor/steel DEMAND WITH NO SUPPLY, one level of the missing industry is created in a coastal state at or beside the leaders capital. Measured against the vanilla 1836 map: GBR already has steel AND engines (Yorkshire), so it needs only the metal shipyard; FRA has steel but no engines, so it needs the yard and a motor works; NET has neither, so it needs all three. Sizes are one level each because the only 1836 steamer consumer is the steam-port stub at 0.7/level - about 28/wk world-wide against 65 from a single shipyard level.
